name: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
definition: Separation of the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium caused by liquefied vitreous passing through one or more full-thickness retinal breaks into the subretinal space; a fresh detachment is convex, corrugated and mobile.

location.notes: Starts at the causative peripheral break (most often a superior or temporal horseshoe tear) and spreads from the ora posteriorly; record extent in clock hours and macula on/off status.

typical_size: 1 clock hour to total (12 clock hours)

drawing.description: Shade the detached area solid blue inside a blue boundary; draw the causative break within it as a blue outline filled red, and a black scalloped line on the ora circle wherever the detachment reaches the ora.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Retinal detachment.

name: Subclinical (localized) retinal detachment
definition: Asymptomatic, localized retinal detachment surrounding a peripheral retinal break, with subretinal fluid confined to the periphery and no symptomatic field loss; it rarely progresses and may regress spontaneously.

location.notes: Around a peripheral atrophic hole or tear near or anterior to the equator; may carry partial pigmented demarcation lines.

typical_size: a few disc diameters around the break; 1–2 clock hours

drawing.description: Small blue-shaded area around the break (break drawn as a blue outline filled red); add a black line on its posterior border if a pigmented demarcation line is present.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Subclinical retinal detachment resulting from asymptomatic retinal breaks: prognosis for progression and regression.
The natural history of asymptomatic retinal breaks.

name: Ora serrata with adjacent detached retina
definition: Chart marking showing that a retinal detachment extends anteriorly to the ora serrata over the involved clock hours.

location.notes: Drawn on the ora serrata (middle) circle over exactly the clock hours where detached retina reaches the ora.

drawing.description: Black scalloped line overlying the ora circle along the detached clock hours.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Retinal detachment.
Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment surgery: A review.

name: Demarcation line (high-water mark)
definition: Curvilinear line of RPE hyperpigmentation (occasionally depigmented) at the junction of detached and attached retina, marking a long-standing detachment or a previous, more extensive position of the subretinal fluid.

location.notes: At the posterior margin of a chronic, usually inferior, detachment, convex toward the posterior pole; several parallel lines (high-water marks) record successive positions; can also form along the dependent edge after pneumatic retinopexy.

typical_size: spans the detachment margin, typically 2–6 clock hours

drawing.description: Solid black line traced along the attached margin of the detachment (or within detached retina for older lines); draw each high-water mark as its own parallel black line.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha): black solid = 'Pigmented demarcation lines at the attached margin of a detached retina or within the detached retina' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

Dedifferentiation of Retinal Pigment Epithelium in a Patient With Chronic Retinal Detachment.
Barrage laser photocoagulation for macula-sparing asymptomatic clinical rhegmatogenous retinal detachments.

name: Intraretinal macrocyst
definition: Large, thin-walled cavity in the outer plexiform layer of chronically detached retina, usually filled with clear fluid and sometimes with blood, seen as a round translucent dome on the detached retina.

location.notes: Within long-standing detached retina, most often in the inferior or peripheral detachment; can lie at the macula; a hemorrhagic cyst can mimic a choroidal mass.

drawing.description: Blue-outlined round dome inside the blue detachment with curved blue stripes across it to show its configuration; fill red if hemorrhagic.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue solid = 'Intra-retinal cysts [with overlying curvilinear stripes to show configuration]' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

Retinal detachment with hemorrhagic intraretinal macrocyst clinically presenting as pseudo-choroidal melanoma.
Case report: An intraretinal macrocyst with crystalline content and retinal detachment.

name: Subretinal bands (subretinal proliferation)
definition: Linear, branching or annular strands of subretinal proliferative tissue derived from RPE and glial cells beneath long-standing detached retina, which can tent the retina and resist reattachment.

location.notes: Beneath the detached retina, often posterior; may encircle the disc ('napkin ring') or run as branching strands; may persist after reattachment.

typical_size: 1 to several disc diameters long; may span quadrants

drawing.description: Draw each band as a yellow line (straight, branching or ring) within the blue detachment, with the retina tented along it.

color_source: Retinal diagram (Dr Sabin Sahu, SlideShare): yellow = 'subretinal fibrosis' https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044

Evaluation of Ab externo subretinal bands removal during pars plana vitrectomy for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment complicated by proliferative vitreoretinopathy.

name: Tractional retinal detachment
definition: Elevation of the retina from the RPE by contraction of preretinal, intraretinal or subretinal fibrovascular/fibrocellular membranes without a retinal break, giving a concave, immobile detachment.

location.notes: Typically along the major vascular arcades and disc in proliferative diabetic retinopathy; concave surface that rarely reaches the ora; may form a 'tabletop' between adhesions or involve the macula.

typical_size: 1–several disc diameters to several clock hours

drawing.description: Shade the concave detached area blue (without ora involvement) and draw the responsible membranes over it in green (orange where vascularized), with lines/arrows showing the direction of traction.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (detached retina blue; elevated neovascularization orange) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) green = 'Vitreous membranes' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

Four-port bimanual 23-gauge vitrectomy for diabetic tractional retinal detachment.

name: Combined tractional-rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
definition: Tractional detachment in which contracting fibrovascular tissue has torn a retinal break, so the detachment becomes convex and more mobile and extends beyond the traction zone, often toward the ora.

location.notes: Traction at the arcades/disc with a small, often posterior break adjacent to fibrovascular adhesions (frequently found only at surgery); detachment commonly involves 3–4 quadrants.

drawing.description: Blue detachment extending beyond the traction zone (black scalloped ora line where it reaches the ora), green/orange membranes at the adhesions, and the break drawn as a blue outline filled red.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) green = 'Vitreous membranes' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Combined rhegmatogenous and traction retinal detachment in proliferative diabetic retinopathy: clinical manifestations and surgical outcome.
Combined Tractional and Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment in Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy in the Anti-VEGF Era.

name: Exudative (serous) retinal detachment
definition: Retinal detachment without a retinal break, caused by subretinal accumulation of exudate when inflammatory, infectious, neoplastic, vascular or choroidal disease breaks down the blood–retinal barrier; the retina is smooth and convex and the fluid shifts with posture.

location.notes: Gravitates to the dependent inferior fundus when upright; bullous, smooth surface without corrugations; the underlying cause (tumour, choroiditis) may be visible.

drawing.description: Smooth blue-shaded bullous area with no break; show the shifted fluid boundary with interrupted blue lines (see shifting subretinal fluid).

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Exudative retinal detachment.
Retinal detachment.
An Unusual Case of Exudative Retinal Detachment in a 6-Year-Old Child with Acute Retinal Necrosis.

name: Shifting subretinal fluid
definition: Change in the location and extent of a (usually exudative) retinal detachment with head position, as subretinal fluid gravitates to the most dependent part of the fundus.

location.notes: Outline the alternate boundary (e.g., supine vs upright) of the detachment; characteristic of exudative RD, uveal effusion and bullous central serous chorioretinopathy.

drawing.description: Interrupted (dashed) blue line showing the changed boundary or folds of the detached retina caused by shifting fluid.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue interrupted lines = 'Outline of change in area or folds of the detached retina because of shifting fluid' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Uveal effusion syndrome.
Bullous Central Serous Chorioretinopathy: A Rare and Atypical Form of Central Serous Chorioretinopathy. A Systematic Review.
Castleman's disease presenting with uveal effusion syndrome.

name: Choroidal detachment (serous / effusion)
definition: Collection of serous fluid in the suprachoroidal space that produces smooth, dome-shaped, brownish elevations of the choroid and overlying retina, usually peripheral and often associated with hypotony.

location.notes: Peripheral, often annular (360°) and lobulated; the ora and ciliary body can be seen without indentation; may accompany rhegmatogenous RD (RRD-CD) or follow surgery/hypotony.

drawing.description: Solid brown dome-shaped lobules drawn from the ora backwards over the involved clock hours; the overlying retina stays red (attached) unless an RD coexists.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): brown solid = 'Choroidal detachment' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; also Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022 (PMID 36190076) https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22

pubmed.title: Uveal effusion syndrome.
COMBINED RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL AND CHOROIDAL DETACHMENT: A Systematic Review.

name: Suprachoroidal hemorrhage (hemorrhagic choroidal detachment)
definition: Accumulation of blood in the suprachoroidal space, occurring spontaneously, during or after intraocular surgery, or after trauma, producing dark red-brown, firm, often very elevated choroidal domes.

location.notes: Peripheral domes that can extend posteriorly; limited (1–2 quadrants) or massive and appositional.

drawing.description: Brown-outlined dome(s) (choroidal detachment) filled red to indicate blood, distinguishing them from brown-filled serous choroidals.

color_source: inferred: brown = choroidal detachment (Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, eOphtha https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology) combined with red = hemorrhage (CMS L33567 App A)

name: Appositional ('kissing') choroidal detachment
definition: Choroidal detachments (serous or hemorrhagic) large enough that opposing bullae meet in the central vitreous cavity, bringing the overlying retinal surfaces into contact.

location.notes: Bullae arise peripherally and touch centrally, usually just in front of the disc, hiding the posterior pole.

typical_size: two or more opposing quadrants, often 360°

drawing.description: Brown domes from opposite quadrants drawn reaching the centre and touching; use red fill with brown outline if hemorrhagic; label 'appositional'.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): brown solid = 'Choroidal detachment' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Vitreous management in massive suprachoroidal hemorrhage.
Spontaneous Resolution of Delayed Suprachoroidal Hemorrhage in the Single Eye Following Needling in Congenital Glaucoma.

name: Retinoschisis-associated retinal detachment (schisis-detachment)
definition: Retinal detachment arising through outer-layer breaks of degenerative retinoschisis, either localized beneath the schisis cavity (schisis-detachment) or progressive and symptomatic when fluid extends beyond the posterior border of the schisis.

location.notes: Under and posterior to bullous peripheral retinoschisis (commonly inferotemporal); outer-layer breaks are often large, round and may be posterior to the equator; localized forms may show pigmented demarcation lines.

drawing.description: Blue-shaded detachment under/behind the schisis; draw the schisis inner layer with a blue outline and blue cross-hatching, and outer-layer breaks with a blue outline filled red.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (detached retina blue) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue cross-lined = 'The inner layer of retinoschisis', red = 'open interior of outer layer holes in retinoschisis' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Detachment / tear of the pars plana epithelium
definition: Separation, often with tearing, of the non-pigmented ciliary epithelium of the pars plana anterior to the ora serrata, typically after blunt trauma, which can cause a shallow, smooth peripheral retinal detachment.

location.notes: In the band between the ora and ciliary-process circles; usually needs scleral depression to see; the associated detachment is shallow and flat-surfaced.

drawing.description: Blue outline with blue cross-hatching in the pars plana band anterior to the ora over the affected clock hours.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue cross-lined = 'Detached pars plana epithelium anterior to the separation of ora serrata' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Star fold (focal fixed fold, PVR)
definition: Fixed retinal folds radiating from a central point, produced by focal contraction of an epiretinal (or subretinal) membrane in proliferative vitreoretinopathy.

location.notes: On detached retina posterior or anterior to the equator, frequently inferior; count clock hours involved for PVR grading.

drawing.description: Short blue lines radiating from a central point on the blue detachment.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue solid = 'Meridional, radial, fixed & circumferential folds' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; CMS L33567 App A short blue lines = folds

name: Fixed retinal folds (diffuse PVR contraction)
definition: Rigid, immobile folds of detached retina caused by diffuse contraction of pre- or subretinal PVR membranes, which can coalesce and shorten the retina.

location.notes: Posterior folds often converge toward the disc; circumferential or radial folds occur near the equator; record clock hours involved.

drawing.description: Solid blue lines tracing each fold (meridional, radial or circumferential) on the blue detachment.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue solid = 'Meridional, radial, fixed & circumferential folds' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: The classification of retinal detachment with proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
An updated classification of retinal detachment with proliferative vitreoretinopathy.

name: Rolled (curled) edge of retinal tear
definition: Inward rolling of the posterior edge or flap of a retinal tear caused by epiretinal cellular proliferation and contraction, a sign of PVR and typical of giant retinal tears.

location.notes: Along the posterior margin of a horseshoe or giant tear; the flap may fold over on itself.

typical_size: length of the tear edge, 1–3 or more clock hours

drawing.description: Curved blue cross-lined band along the posterior edge of the break, with the break itself drawn as a blue outline filled red.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue cross-lined = 'Rolled edges of retinal tears [curved lines]' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Cryopexy in primary rhegmatogenous retinal detachment: a risk factor for postoperative proliferative vitreoretinopathy?

name: Epiretinal proliferation / PVR membrane
definition: Contractile fibrocellular membrane on the inner retinal surface formed in proliferative vitreoretinopathy or after detachment repair, causing surface wrinkling, vessel tortuosity and traction folds.

location.notes: On detached or reattached retina; commonly the macula after RD repair and the inferior retina in PVR.

typical_size: 1 disc diameter to several clock hours

drawing.description: Green-outlined area with fine green wavy lines indicating surface wrinkling; add blue fold lines where it drags the retina.

color_source: Jayanna & Shanmugam, 'It is time for more colors!' Indian J Ophthalmol 2022 (PMID 36190076): preretinal lesions incl. epiretinal membrane coded green https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22

name: Anterior PVR (circumferential contraction / anterior displacement)
definition: Contraction of proliferative membranes on the residual vitreous base that drags the peripheral retina centrally and anteriorly toward the ciliary body or iris, producing circumferential and radial fixed folds and a peripheral trough.

location.notes: At the vitreous base between the equator and ora, extending onto the pars plana/ciliary body; most common inferiorly after vitrectomy or trauma; record clock hours.

drawing.description: Green band along the vitreous base for the contracted membrane, with short blue radial fold lines just posterior to it; add an anterior arrow for anterior displacement.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green = 'Vitreous membranes', blue = 'Meridional, radial, fixed & circumferential folds' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

Anterior proliferative vitreoretinopathy in the silicone study. Silicone Study Report Number 10.

name: Funnel retinal detachment (advanced PVR)
definition: Total retinal detachment in which fixed folds in all quadrants shorten the retina into an open, narrow or closed funnel (Retina Society PVR grade D).

location.notes: Whole fundus; folds converge on the disc; the posterior pole may be hidden in a closed funnel.

drawing.description: Entire fundus shaded blue with blue fold lines converging on the disc and a black scalloped line along the whole ora; annotate funnel type.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (detached retina blue; ora with detached retina) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) blue folds https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: The classification of retinal detachment with proliferative vitreoretinopathy.

name: Posterior vitreous detachment (posterior hyaloid)
definition: Separation of the posterior cortical vitreous (posterior hyaloid) from the internal limiting membrane, beginning in the perifoveal macula and completed when it separates from the optic disc.

location.notes: Mobile membrane in front of the posterior pole; record complete vs partial and any persisting adhesion (macula, disc, vessels, tear flap).

drawing.description: Curved green line in front of the posterior pole for the detached hyaloid face, with attachment points shown where it still adheres.

color_source: Retinal diagram (Dr Sabin Sahu, SlideShare): green = 'Vitreous detachment (Weiss ring)' https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044

name: Weiss ring
definition: Ring-shaped condensation of peripapillary glial tissue torn from the optic disc margin and suspended in the posterior hyaloid, the classic sign of complete posterior vitreous detachment.

location.notes: Floats in the vitreous in front of the optic disc and moves with eye movement.

drawing.description: Small green ring drawn over or just in front of the optic disc.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green solid = 'Hyaloid ring' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; Retinal diagram (Dr Sabin Sahu, SlideShare) green = Weiss ring https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044

name: Vitreous hemorrhage
definition: Extravasated blood within the vitreous gel or retrohyaloid space, most often from proliferative diabetic retinopathy, a retinal tear, neovascularization after vein occlusion, or PVD without a tear.

location.notes: Diffuse or localized; older blood settles inferiorly and dehemoglobinizes to yellow-white; record density and the area of fundus obscured.

drawing.description: Shade the area of fundus obscured by hemorrhage green (lighter shading for less dense hemorrhage).

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Red blood in vitreous (fresh clot)
definition: Fresh, red (not yet dehemoglobinized) blood or clot visible in the vitreous cavity, distinguished on the chart from older dispersed vitreous hemorrhage.

location.notes: Over the bleeding source (tear, neovascular frond) or as a clot in the vitreous, often inferior.

typical_size: small clot to several clock hours

drawing.description: Green outline filled red over the clot or fresh blood.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Vitreous Hemorrhage.

name: Subhyaloid / preretinal hemorrhage
definition: Blood trapped between the posterior hyaloid (or ILM) and the retina, forming a dark red, sharply bounded, often boat-shaped collection with a flat upper fluid level that hides the underlying retina.

location.notes: Premacular or along the arcades/neovascular fronds; red cells settle inferiorly to give a horizontal upper meniscus (D shape).

typical_size: 1–8 disc diameters (mean ~6 DD in a YAG hyaloidotomy series)

drawing.description: Solid red D-shaped area with a straight horizontal upper border.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): red solid = 'Haemorrhages (pre-retinal and intra-retinal)' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; CMS L33567 App A red = hemorrhages

name: Vitreous membrane / vitreoretinal traction band
definition: Condensed or fibrotic sheet or strand of vitreous that inserts on the retina and transmits traction, seen as a grey-white membrane crossing the vitreous cavity.

location.notes: Draw its course through the vitreous to its retinal insertion (tear flap, lattice, neovascular frond, macula, disc).

typical_size: variable; may span the posterior pole to the periphery

drawing.description: Solid green line(s) or sheet outline ending at the retinal insertion; add an arrow for the direction of traction.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green solid = 'Vitreous membranes' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022 (PMID 36190076)

name: Fibrovascular proliferation (fibrovascular membrane)
definition: Neovascular fronds with accompanying fibrous tissue growing from the disc or retina onto the posterior hyaloid (e.g., in proliferative diabetic retinopathy), whose contraction causes vitreous hemorrhage and tractional detachment.

location.notes: Along the major vascular arcades and on the optic disc, often with broad plaque-like adhesions at several sites.

typical_size: 1/4 disc diameter to several clock hours along the arcades

drawing.description: Orange-filled (elevated neovascularization) frond with a green outline for its elevated fibrous component; involuted, purely fibrous tissue drawn in green only.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (orange = elevated neovascularization) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green = 'Outline of elevated NV' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Asteroid hyalosis
definition: Numerous small white-to-cream spherical calcium-phosphate (hydroxyapatite) bodies suspended in and moving with the vitreous gel, usually unilateral and asymptomatic.

location.notes: Diffusely distributed in the gel; bodies move with the vitreous and return to position rather than settling; can obscure the fundus view.

drawing.description: Green stippled area over the part of the fundus obscured.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green stippled = asteroid hyalosis https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022 (PMID 36190076)

name: Synchysis scintillans (cholesterolosis bulbi)
definition: Refractile golden cholesterol crystals floating freely in liquefied vitreous that settle inferiorly when the eye is still, typically after long-standing vitreous hemorrhage, trauma, chronic inflammation or chronic retinal detachment.

location.notes: Swirl up with eye movement, then sink to the inferior vitreous cavity.

drawing.description: Scattered green dots concentrated over the inferior fundus; label to distinguish from asteroid hyalosis.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (green = opacities in media); dot pattern inferred to distinguish from asteroid hyalosis

name: Vitreous cells / haze (vitritis)
definition: Inflammatory cells, protein or pigment clumps in the vitreous that reduce the clarity of the fundus view, graded clinically on the standardized (SUN) vitreous haze scale.

location.notes: Diffuse or localized over an inflammatory focus; record the grade (0–4+).

drawing.description: Green stippling over the hazy area, denser for higher grades; annotate the haze grade.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (green = opacities in media)

pubmed.title: Standardization of uveitis nomenclature for reporting clinical data. Results of the First International Workshop.

name: Intraocular foreign body
definition: Retained foreign material that has penetrated the globe and lies in the vitreous cavity or is embedded in the retina/choroid, often with vitreous hemorrhage and a retinal impact site.

location.notes: Free in the vitreous (often inferior) or impacted on the posterior retina; draw the entry track and retinal impact site.

typical_size: <1 to several mm (draw to scale against the disc)

drawing.description: Solid green shape at the foreign-body position; mark its track as a green line and the retinal impact site (red hemorrhage, blue-outlined red break).

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green solid = 'IOFB' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022 (PMID 36190076)

pubmed.title: Ferrous intraocular foreign bodies retained in the posterior segment: management options and results.

name: Retained (dropped) lens fragment
definition: Nuclear, epinuclear or cortical lens material dislocated into the vitreous cavity during cataract surgery, often lying on the inferior retina with intraocular inflammation and raised pressure.

location.notes: Usually rests on the inferior retina or posterior pole, sometimes enveloped by vitreous.

drawing.description: Green-outlined, green cross-hatched opacity at its position; label 'nucleus' or 'cortex'.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (green = opacities in media); cross-hatching inferred to distinguish from IOFB

name: Vitreous base avulsion
definition: Traumatic tearing of the vitreous base from the retina and/or pars plana, seen as a ribbon-like ('bucket-handle') band suspended in the anterior vitreous, often with peripheral tears or dialysis.

location.notes: Hangs in the anterior vitreous parallel to the ora, may carry strips of pars plana epithelium or retina; follows blunt trauma (e.g., squash-ball injury series with tears near the ora).

drawing.description: Curved green band drawn just central to the ora circle over the affected clock hours.

color_source: inferred: green = preretinal/vitreous lesions (Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022, PMID 36190076, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

name: Encircling scleral buckle (band)
definition: Silicone band sutured 360° around the globe beneath the rectus muscles, indenting the sclera to support the vitreous base and retinal breaks and relieve circumferential traction.

location.notes: Circumferential 360° ridge typically at or just anterior to the equator; segmental elements may be added beneath breaks.

drawing.description: Two parallel circumferential lines around the equator marking the buckle edges: black where the retina is attached, brown where the buckle lies under detached retina.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black = 'Edge of buckle beneath the attached retina', brown = 'Edge of buckle beneath the detached retina' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Segmental (circumferential) scleral buckle
definition: Silicone sponge or solid tire sutured limbus-parallel over a limited arc to indent the sclera beneath one or more retinal breaks.

location.notes: Over the clock hours of the breaks, extending beyond them on each side, usually between the equator and ora; may be combined with vitrectomy for inferior breaks.

drawing.description: Two parallel circumferential lines over the involved clock hours with closed ends: black under attached retina, brown under detached retina.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): buckle edge black (attached) / brown (detached) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Radial sponge (meridional buckle)
definition: Sponge explant sutured perpendicular to the limbus (meridionally) beneath a large horseshoe tear to close it while avoiding fishmouthing and radial folds.

location.notes: Radially oriented beneath the tear, from near the ora extending posterior to the tear's posterior edge.

typical_size: about 1 clock hour wide; 2–4 disc diameters long

drawing.description: Two parallel radial lines beneath the tear with a closed posterior end: black under attached retina, brown under detached retina.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): buckle edge black (attached) / brown (detached) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Fishmouthing / radial fold on buckle
definition: Radial retinal fold arising from redundant retina over a circumferential buckle that holds a tear open ('fishmouthing') and can leak, typically with large horseshoe tears on limbus-parallel buckles.

location.notes: Runs radially across the circumferential buckle, posteriorly from the gaping tear.

drawing.description: Short blue radial lines across the buckle for the fold; the open tear drawn as a blue outline filled red, gaping at its posterior lip.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (short blue lines = meridional folds; blue outline filled red = full-thickness break)

name: Scleral buckle intrusion
definition: Late erosion of a scleral buckle element through the sclera and choroid into the eye, seen as a smooth grey-white element beneath or through the retina at the buckle site.

location.notes: At the buckle site; may be an incidental finding decades after surgery.

drawing.description: Black-outlined segment of the buckle filled white where the element is visible intraocularly.

color_source: inferred: buckle edge black (Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, eOphtha https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology); white fill for exposed implant

name: Laser retinopexy around a break
definition: Two to three rows of confluent photocoagulation burns surrounding a retinal break (and any cuff of fluid) to create a chorioretinal adhesion; healed burns become pigmented scars with atrophic centres.

location.notes: Encircles the break on attached retina; anteriorly the rows may be carried to the ora.

typical_size: ring 1–2 disc diameters wider than the break

drawing.description: Rows of small black dots (healed, pigmented burns) encircling the break; draw fresh burns in yellow.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black solid = 'Hyperpigmentation as a result of the previous treatment with Cryo/PHC/Diathermy' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Laser demarcation (barrier) line
definition: Two to three confluent rows of photocoagulation placed on attached retina along the posterior border of a localized detachment to limit its posterior spread.

location.notes: Curved line posterior to the detachment margin on attached retina, with both ends carried to the ora.

drawing.description: Curved band of 2–3 rows of black dots on attached retina just posterior to the blue detachment, ends reaching the ora.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black = treatment hyperpigmentation after PHC https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: 360° peripheral laser retinopexy
definition: Confluent rows of photocoagulation applied circumferentially around the whole peripheral retina, usually anterior to the equator, as prophylaxis against (re)detachment after vitrectomy or before silicone oil removal.

location.notes: 360° band between the equator and ora.

drawing.description: Continuous circumferential band of black dots between the equator and ora circles.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black = treatment hyperpigmentation after PHC https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) scars
definition: Scatter laser burns placed across the mid- and peripheral retina outside the vascular arcades for proliferative ischemic retinopathy, healing as pigmented chorioretinal scars that can enlarge over time.

location.notes: Outside the arcades and nasal to the disc, sparing the macula and papillomacular bundle, out to and beyond the equator; sectoral PRP is limited to an ischemic sector.

drawing.description: Scattered black dots filling the mid-periphery outside the arcades, leaving the posterior pole clear.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black = treatment hyperpigmentation after PHC https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Focal / grid macular laser scars
definition: Small laser burns applied to leaking microaneurysms (focal) or in a grid over thickened macula for diabetic macular edema, sparing the foveal centre; healed burns appear as small pigmented or atrophic spots.

location.notes: Within the arcades, sparing the foveal centre; scars may enlarge with time.

typical_size: small spots over a 1–3 disc diameter area

drawing.description: Small black dots in the treated macular area, leaving the fovea clear.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black = treatment hyperpigmentation after PHC https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Fresh laser (photocoagulation) burns
definition: Recently applied laser burns visible as grey-white spots of outer-retinal whitening and edema that later pigment into scars.

location.notes: Wherever treatment was applied at this visit; redraw as black scars at follow-up.

typical_size: spots ~100–500 µm in rows or scatter

drawing.description: Yellow dots/rows at the treated positions to show fresh, edematous burns.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): yellow solid = 'Post-PHC retinal edema' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Cryopexy (cryotherapy) scar
definition: Chorioretinal scar from transscleral freezing around a retinal break, appearing acutely as white frosting and later as larger, irregular patches of pigment clumping and RPE atrophy.

location.notes: Around peripheral breaks, often on the buckle; applications are contiguous around the break.

typical_size: each application about 1–2 disc diameters; confluent around the break

drawing.description: Black-outlined patches with black stippled pigment around the break; fresh cryo (white frost) may be drawn yellow.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black solid = 'Hyperpigmentation as a result of the previous treatment with Cryo/PHC/Diathermy' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: External subretinal fluid drainage site
definition: Site of transscleral choroidotomy used to drain subretinal fluid during buckling surgery, later visible as a small pigmented chorioretinal scar, sometimes with local subretinal hemorrhage or retinal incarceration.

location.notes: Beneath or beside the buckle where subretinal fluid was deepest, usually between rectus muscles.

drawing.description: Small black X at the drainage site; add red if subretinal hemorrhage is present.

color_source: inferred: black = pigmented chorioretinal scar after treatment (Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, eOphtha https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology); X symbol for a point site

name: Drainage retinotomy
definition: Small iatrogenic full-thickness retinal opening made during vitrectomy to drain subretinal fluid, usually surrounded by endolaser and visible postoperatively as a round hole within a pigmented laser ring.

location.notes: Usually in the mid-periphery away from the macula, in an area of deep subretinal fluid.

drawing.description: Small full-thickness break (blue outline filled red) surrounded by a ring of black laser dots.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (blue outline filled red = full-thickness break) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) black treatment scars https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Relaxing retinotomy / retinectomy edge
definition: Surgical incision or excision of contracted, shortened retina (usually peripheral and circumferential) to relieve PVR traction, leaving a free posterior retinal edge secured with endolaser and bare RPE/choroid anteriorly.

location.notes: Most often inferior, 90–180° (up to 360°), anterior to the equator; the posterior edge can fold or slip.

drawing.description: Blue line marking the retinectomy edge, the area anterior to it treated as a giant break (blue outline filled red), and 2–3 rows of black laser dots just posterior to the edge.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) black treatment scars https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Intraocular gas bubble (air / SF6 / C3F8)
definition: Intravitreal air or expansile gas (SF6, C2F6, C3F8) used as internal tamponade after vitrectomy or pneumatic retinopexy, seen as a mobile superior bubble with a horizontal inferior meniscus.

location.notes: Rises to the highest point of the cavity; record % fill and meniscus level; positioning places it against the break.

drawing.description: Green outline of the bubble over the superior fundus bounded by a straight horizontal meniscus line; annotate gas type and % fill.

color_source: inferred: no established colour for tamponades (Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022, PMID 36190076, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22); green used for vitreous-cavity contents per CMS L33567 App A (opacities in media) and PMID 36190076 (preretinal = green)

name: Pneumatic retinopexy
definition: Office repair combining intravitreal expansile gas injection with cryopexy or laser to the break(s) and head positioning so the bubble tamponades the break, classically for breaks within the superior 8 clock hours.

location.notes: Classic indication: single break or group of breaks no larger than 1 clock hour in the superior 8 clock hours; the bubble is positioned over the break.

typical_size: break(s) ≤1 clock hour; bubble occupies the superior cavity

drawing.description: Superior gas bubble outlined green with retinopexy marks around the break (black dots or stipple, yellow if fresh); note any new breaks and dependent demarcation line.

color_source: inferred: tamponade drawn green (see intraocular gas bubble; PMID 36190076) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) black treatment scars https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Silicone oil tamponade
definition: Long-term intravitreal tamponade with silicone oil (lighter or heavier than water) after vitrectomy for complex detachments, showing a glistening reflex at its meniscus and usually requiring later removal.

location.notes: Fills most of the cavity; standard oil floats (inferior aqueous rim), heavy oil sinks (superior aqueous rim); mark under-fill and any oil-retina interface.

drawing.description: Green outline of the oil bubble with light green parallel hatching; mark the meniscus (inferior for standard oil, superior for heavy oil) and label 'SO'.

color_source: inferred: no established colour for silicone oil (Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022, PMID 36190076, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22); green for vitreous-cavity contents per CMS L33567 App A; hatching distinguishes oil from gas

name: Emulsified silicone oil droplets
definition: Dispersion of silicone oil into small droplets after prolonged tamponade, seen as tiny refractile bubbles in the vitreous cavity (and as an inverted pseudohypopyon in the anterior chamber) that may adhere to the retina.

location.notes: Droplets of standard oil gather superiorly in the cavity and on the retinal surface.

typical_size: droplets far smaller than the disc, often diffuse

drawing.description: Clusters of small green dots/circles where droplets are seen, mainly superiorly.

color_source: inferred: tamponade/vitreous contents drawn green (CMS L33567 App A opacities in media; PMID 36190076)

name: Retained perfluorocarbon liquid (PFCL) droplet
definition: Residual droplet(s) of heavy perfluorocarbon liquid left after vitrectomy, seen as clear, round, highly refractile bubbles that sink to the dependent vitreous cavity or become trapped subretinally, often beneath the fovea.

location.notes: Preretinal droplets lie in the most dependent cavity; subretinal droplets sit under the posterior pole/fovea and can migrate.

drawing.description: Small round green-outlined circle(s) at the droplet position; label 'PFCL' and 'subretinal' when beneath the retina.

color_source: inferred: no established colour for perfluoro liquids (Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022, PMID 36190076, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22); green for tamponade per CMS L33567 App A opacities in media

name: Postoperative retinal (macular) fold
definition: Fold of the reattached retina, sometimes crossing the macula, caused by residual subretinal fluid displaced by gas tamponade or by retinal slippage after detachment repair.

location.notes: Usually across the posterior pole/macula after gas tamponade; can be associated with macular translocation, diplopia and metamorphopsia; may flatten spontaneously.

drawing.description: Blue line along the course of the fold on attached retina.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): blue solid = 'Meridional, radial, fixed & circumferential folds' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology
